_about: Comparison rows and source links for the dashboards' What-if panels. Text and numbers copied from submission/IMPACT.md (another worker's file); merged into /shared/impact.json at build time.

compare: AEMET warnings
Red weather warning by zone at about 7:30 AM, a 12-hour gap before phones were alerted. A warning isn't an instruction to the public.
Turns the rain signal into a drafted, town-specific alert with what to do, ready to send (simulated).
EFAS / GloFAS
Flood-probability notices to agencies by email, up to 48 h ahead; not binding, and it underestimated the size.
Doesn't replace forecasts. Adds observed NASA rain + radar evidence on one screen with a task queue, so a notice becomes an action.
ES-Alert
Sent at about 8 PM with "avoid travel" only.
Pre-fills the message and the target towns from the map (simulated; no real ES-Alert link).
Copernicus EMS rapid mapping
First maps 31 Oct; province-wide extent 2 Nov.
Open NASA OPERA radar water every pass, linked to rain and simulated dispatch. Complements EMS; not faster for the first map.
NASA FIRMS
Active fires within about 3 h of a pass: where it's burning now.
Harmonizes MODIS (2000–) and VIIRS (2012–) into one 26-year, single-scale record so seasons can be compared and trends tested.
CWFIS (Natural Resources Canada)
Daily national fire weather and behaviour maps; not designed for operational fire management.
Adds the multi-year, per-province view (is May getting worse here?) and a simulated pre-season task list.
Readiness by fixed date
Alberta: full staffing by 1 May, moved to 15 April for 2024.
Sets the date from the province's own satellite record of unusual months, reviewed every winter.
USDA NASS Cropland Data Layer
The best map of what was planted, released about February of the next year (75–82% accuracy).
Predicts next season per pixel, before planting (0.8176, one county, one seed: a different task, so not directly comparable).
NASS Prospective Plantings / Crop Progress
State-level surveys (31 March) and weekly state progress.
Field-level, with the climate trend (frost-free days, soil water) attached.
Cover-crop programs
Cost-share by application.
Ranks the fields where rye pays off most (steep, erosion-prone).
sources: U.S. Census Bureau QuickFacts, Iowa (2010 population 3,046,355)
